trigger: a C++ range reaches review without a recorded ownership inventory
classification_rationale: the Gate 1 Resource Ledger is a required statement on every C++ diff; this row records it for this range, independently proven by cpp-safety in governance r1
summary: Gate 1 Resource Ledger (C++) for 5eb783dd4..d880cc982, plus the governance fix round. No new or modified owning raw fd, HANDLE, SOCKET, FILE*, sqlite3 object, mapped library, subprocess or temp path. Owners: (1) PgPool Lease from pool_.try_acquire_for or with_txn_for: the lease is RAII; every early return in the ingest transaction lambda releases through the pool and a failed statement rolls back (PgTxn). In get_device_ci_sections the lease is acquired with try_acquire_for, nothing runs in between, and it is moved into with_txn_on exactly once and never reused. (2) PgResult from exec_params / PQexec: RAII, cleared at scope exit on every return path; PQgetvalue strings are copied into std::string before the result is destroyed. (3) pg::to_text_array takes string_view elements borrowed from backing std::vector<std::string> storage (ords, arrays, record sections) that outlives the call; no view escapes the insert statement. (4) sha256_hex uses an EVP_Digest one-shot into a stack buffer: no EVP_MD_CTX is allocated, nothing to free; failure yields nullopt, mapped to blob_version 2 with an empty hash. (5) The ingest failure diagnostic copies PQerrorMessage into a std::string inside the lambda, first line only, before the connection is released. (6) Test only: the competing-replacements case runs three std::thread (reader, two writers) default-constructed and joined by a scope-exit guard declared before any is started, plus a std::latch; no jthread, no detached thread, every wait bounded (reader capped at kMaxReads, latch released by the reader on every exit path). No callback context, no subprocess, no temp path (PgTestTemplate clones only).
